questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle cannot completely clear the tracks on the other side.
The crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle cannot completely clear the tracks on the other side.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going either direction. Do not stop on the tracks. Make sure your vehicle fully crosses the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly due to darkness or bad weather, stay farther behind other vehicles. This gives you more time to react if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold tablets with alcohol or codeine, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Road work or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of construction, maintenance, and utility work. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe in these areas. Traffic fines may be doubled in areas marked by these signs.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how they absorb alcohol. Other factors include biological sex, how much food is in their digestive tract, and how many drinks they had. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.
Improve traffic flow.
Use good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, driving too slowly can block traffic and result in a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for quick braking or turning.
Helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for quick braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. By looking ahead, you can drive safer, use less fuel, and help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: If there is a large puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to drive through the water.
Go around the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral as you go through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go around the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of touching the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the center, passing is allowed from the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black letters means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-lane road where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below the headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Cars that are passing.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming cars going straight. Turn left only when it is safe and you will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. You need good judgment to drive safely and react to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can hurt your driving ability.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror removes all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots even with mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you need more following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more likely to be fatal. Higher speeds also increase your stopping distance, so you need more space between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be careful.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after stopping.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means do not turn in that direction. Stop and wait for a green light.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians in a crosswalk cross the street. Wait until the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: The broken yellow line means you can pass. The solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed, you have enough space to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
It gets the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous because they occupy your hands, eyes, and mind. Even good drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, in rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. The best way to let others know you are there is to turn:

options.text: Up the dashboard lights.
On your parking lights.
On your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: On your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Use low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.
